name: Nether-lace Garment
summary: At the Crossroads, Kil'hala weaves dryad hair into enchanted cloth for spellcasters. The finished garment marks the end of his specialized work in the Barrens.

sections.title: Weaving the Nether-Lace
sections.body: At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Kil'hala weaves nether-lace from the locks of laughing sisters. The dryads live in Ashenvale, and their hair is harvested for this work. Kil'hala binds the woodland enchantment in those rare, magically resonant locks into cloth that is comfortable and durable.

sections.title: Favors for Orgrimmar
sections.body: Kil'hala wants more than fine work from his trade. He hopes to win favor with Deino, a respected troll mage who lives in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. By making exceptional garb for aspiring practitioners, he hopes to earn and keep Deino's good graces.

faq.answer: Nether-lace is an enchanted fabric Kil'hala weaves from the tresses of laughing sisters. The cloth is resilient and carries their woodland enchantment.
Kil'hala crafts the garment at his station in the Crossroads in the Barrens, once he has the needed dryad hair from Ashenvale.
Deino is an influential troll mage trainer in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. Kil'hala hopes to keep her favor, and believes your satisfaction with his tailoring will reflect well on him.

faq.q: Where did the materials for the garment come from?
faq.answer: The garment's core material is hair gathered from the elusive laughing sisters, dryads found across Ashenvale's forests.

faq.q: Who is this garment made for?
faq.answer: The garment is made chiefly for spellcasters, especially mages in training who need robes that channel arcane energies without hindering movement.
Kil'hala lives at the Crossroads, the central crossroads settlement in the heart of the Barrens.

angles.text: As a mage, you receive a garment that bridges wilderness trials in Ashenvale with Kil'hala's craftsmanship under Deino's guidance.
As a tailor, you can see how exotic reagents such as dryad hair become cloth with innate magical protection.
As a member of the Horde, you help equip its spellcasters with materials from Kalimdor's sacred woods, part of the ongoing contest between the Horde and Ashenvale's woodland defenders.
